chief_complaint: Follow-up for chronic cardiovascular disease, hyperlipidemia, and colorectal polyp surveillance
history_of_present_illness: The 70-year-old male has a long history of myocardial infarction (1998) and persistent hyperlipidemia, for which he is on multiple statins. He is on antihypertensive therapy (hydrochlorothiazide/lisinopril and metoprolol) despite no recent blood pressure recordings. Prediabetes (A1c 6.3%) and chronic anemia have been present since the early 1980s. He has recurrent rectal and colonic polyps diagnosed since 2014, requiring ongoing surveillance. Chronic pain, intractable migraine, sinusitis, and dental issues contribute to frequent healthcare encounters, including several resolved overdoses in the past two years. Social factors include part-time employment, low educational attainment, social isolation, and ongoing drug dependence, which complicate adherence and overall health management.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple lacerations (2024), several drug overdoses (2021, 2023), acute cystitis (2021), gingivitis (2021), and prior full-time employment. The patient also has a longstanding history of myocardial infarction, hyperlipidemia, chronic anemia, prediabetes, chronic pain, migraine, sinusitis, dental disease, and substance dependence.

active_medications.name: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 MG / Lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet

social_determinants: Lives in Milford, MA; part-time employment; primary school education only; social isolation; chronic stress; ongoing dependent drug abuse; limited health literacy.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular: Prior MI, hyperlipidemia, presumed hypertension, prediabetes, and unknown smoking status place the patient at very high risk for recurrent ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and peripheral vascular disease. Renal: ACE‑inhibitor use suggests concern for hypertension or CKD, but eGFR and albuminuria are missing, raising uncertainty about CKD risk. Metabolic: Prediabetes (A1c 6.3%) confers elevated risk of progression to type‑2 diabetes. Hematologic: Chronic anemia may worsen cardiac workload and could be related to CKD or occult GI bleeding from polyps. Neurologic: Vascular risk factors (age, hypertension, dyslipidemia) increase risk for stroke and vascular cognitive impairment.

data_quality_flags.issue: Missing latest systolic blood pressure; hypertension status cannot be confirmed.
Body mass index not recorded; obesity risk unknown.
Renal function (eGFR) not available; CKD stage cannot be assessed.

clinical_impression: Elderly male with significant cardiovascular disease burden, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, prediabetes, chronic anemia, and ongoing colorectal polyp surveillance, complicated by substance dependence and social determinants that may affect adherence and outcomes.
